findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The sanitizer dispenser in the Winter utility closet was observed to be dispensing no measurable concentration of sanitizer. CORRECTED- maintenance was able to reconnect a hose that had come loose. Dispenser was observed to be releasing 400 ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure frequent testing of chemical sanitizers to ensure the proper concentration as recommended by the manufacturer’s label.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: The test strips in the Reach kitchen were observed to have expired in 2021. CORRECTED- new sanitizer test strips were brought to each care center kitchen. Test kits must be available and functioning (periodically check expiration dates) to test the concentration of chemical sanitizers used for food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided. [Pf]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed an accumulation of food and other debris in the following areas:
1) The corner cabinet in Summer.
2) Along the freezer gasket in Winter.
3) Along the freezer gasket in Spring.
4) In containers holding clean utensils in Spring.
5) In containers holding clean utensils in Reach.
6) The top of the Care Center dish machine.
Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Inspector observed opened milk containers in both the Reach and Spring kitchen to be missing date marking. The person in charge (PIC) verified that they were opened within the past 1-2 days. CORRECTED- the date the items were opened was placed on the containers. Ensure all temperature control for food safety (TCS) foods are date marked if held for over 24 hours. The date of opening/ preparation/ thawing counts as day one.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A). [P]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed an unmarked bottle of clear liquid in the mop room of the Spring kitchen. The PIC was unable to verify the contents. CORRECTED- the bottle was emptied and brought to the main kitchen for ware washing. Ensure all clear liquids, chemicals, and cleaning products are labeled to prevent potential chemical contamination of foods or food contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. [Pf[

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: The kitchen sanitizer bucket in the “Winter” wing was observed with no measurable sanitizer concentration. CORRECTED- sanitizer bucket was remade and observed to be at a proper concentration of 400ppm quaternary ammonia. Ensure sanitizer buckets are changed at a frequency to hold proper concentration levels as recommended by the manufacturer's label.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (2) Have a concentration of 200-400 ppm and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. [P]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Inspector observed food debris or dust in the following locations:
1) Food debris in the silverware divider in “Spring” kitchen
2) Food debris in the silverware divider in “Winter” kitchen
3) Dust and soil accumulation on top of the Care Center dish machine. 
Ensure nonfood contact surfaces are cleaned at a frequency to prevent the accumulation of dust, soil, and food debris.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a leak on the front right edge of the Care Center’s dish machine during the rinse cycle. The person in charge (PIC) was notified and will be making a call to EcoLab to have the machine serviced. Ensure plumbing systems are maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Inspector and PIC observed holes in the walls (appeared as through shelving units had been relocated) of the mop sink rooms in each branch of the Care Center. The PIC noted the repairs to be made by maintenance. Ensure physical facilities are maintained in good repair.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Slight soil accumulation was observed in the Memory Care and Spring ice machines. Ensure the interiors of ice machines are cleaned regularly to prevent soil accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.11(E) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (E) Except when dry cleaning methods are used as specified under § 4-603.11, surfaces of UTENSILS and EQUIPMENT contacting FOOD that is not TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be cleaned: (4) In EQUIPMENT such as ice bins and BEVERAGE dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of EQUIPMENT such as ice makers, cooking oil storage tanks and distribution lines, BEVERAGE and syrup dispensing lines or tubes, coffee bean grinders, and water vending EQUIPMENT: (a) At a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or (b) Absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: MEMORY CARE: The kitchen sanitizer bucket was observed with no measurable sanitizer concentration. The concentrated sanitizer jug on the dispenser was observed to be low and incapable of dispensing proeprly. CORRECTED- PIC replaced the concentrated jug with a new one. Sanitizer was then dispensed at 400ppm quat.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (2) Have a concentration of 200-400 ppm and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. [P]

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
Dishwasher temperature logs in the SPRING Care Center were not available. Inspector will follow up to see that staff have been trained on how to properly complete the logs, and that the logs are being regularly and accurately completed.
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16. [Pf]

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
Probe thermometers in the SUMMER kitchen were not accurate. One thermometer read 0F at room temperature. Another thermometer ready 35F when in ice water. CORRECTED- Thermometers were calibrated using ice water. Check thermometer calibration on a regular basis to ensure they are accurate to +/-2F.
4-203.11: (A) FOOD TEMP. MEASURING DEVICE shall be accurate to  +/- 1 Celsius (B) accurate to +/- 2 Fahrenheit.  [Pf]

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
Dishwasher temperature logs in the Memory Care Center were not available. Inspector will follow up to see that staff have been trained on how to properly complete the logs, and that the logs are being regularly and accurately completed.
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16. [Pf]

findings.title: Charge present, demonstrates knowledge, and performs duties
findings.comment:
Dishwasher temperature logs in the Memory Care Center were found to be falsified. Logs for most of the month of August were already completed during this inspection (on August 1st). Inspector will follow up to see that staff have been trained on how to properly complete the logs, and again in several months to see that the logs are being regularly and accurately completed.
2-102.11: Based on the RISKS inherent to the FOOD operation, PIC shall demonstrate knowledge by:  (A) Having no Priority Foundation items; (B) Being a CFM; OR (C) Responding correctly questions as they relate to the specific FOOD operation. The areas of knowledge include C1 through C16. [Pf]

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
Forks and spoons observed at the Summer Care Center with food contact ends out. CORRECTED- Utensils were removed from the service counter. Discussed proper utensil storage (eating ends down). 
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. [C]

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.11 Food service staff working in Memory Care wing were unable to properly wash hands at the designated handwashing sink in the kitchen based on conditions observed. Pump bottle of hand sanitizer was present at the handwashing sink, and the automatic soap dispenser was not working properly (see #10 for details). Servers were noted to have washed their hands in the restroom prior to serving residents, which would require touching general surfaces not considered to be clean prior to service. Proper handwashing at the designated handwashing sink in the kitchen prior to service and between tasks was discussed. 
Food employees shall keep their hands and exposed portions of their arms clean.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.11 1. Automatic soap dispenser at handwashing sink in Memory Care kitchen was not functioning properly. A part was broken inside the dispenser that allows soap to dispense when activated. Maintenance changed the soap dispenser during inspection, and new dispenser functioned properly.
2. Soap would not dispense from automatic soap dispenser in the dish room. Batteries were changed to allow for proper function of the soap dispenser.
Each handwashing sink shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:
4-302.12 Food thermometer was not present at Memory Care kitchen. PIC provided new thermometer during inspection.
Food temperature measuring devices shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of food temperatures.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 Employee working in Spring Hill kitchen did not wash hands between taking a drink from a personal beverage and putting on gloves to continue with next task. Handwashing between tasks and prior to putting on gloves were discussed. Employee was observed washing hands properly between tasks for remainder of inspection.
Food Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles, after handling soiled equipment and utensils, before putting on gloves, and after engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Mold was observed in the Summer Breeze, Spring Hill, and Reach kitchen ice machines on front surfaces around the ice maker covers. Mold was also observed on the sides of the water trough in back of the Summer Breeze ice machine. Ensure ice machines are cleaned and sanitized as needed to prevent mold growth.
Equipment such as ice bins and enclosed components, such as ice makers, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-102.11 Spray bottle in the Memory Care kitchen was observed with a label indicting it was QT 3 hard surface disinfectant. Employee working in Memory Care stated the bottle contained Re-Juv-Nal quat sanitizer that is used in the kitchens. Proper labeling was discussed, and employee stated they would relabel the bottle. Although QT 3 and Re-Juv-Nal are both quat products they have different intended uses. QT 3 is a hard surface disinfectant and Re-Juv-Nal is sanitizer intended for use in kitchens. Make sure chemicals are in properly labeled spray bottles and used appropriately based on the intended use of chemicals.
Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Evidence was observed to indicate a handwashing sink was used as a dump sink. Ice cubes were observed in the basin of the Memory Care kitchen handwashing sink. Manager was advised to speak with all staff about proper use of handwashing sinks. 
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Cease the practice of using handwashing sinks as dump sinks.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Ice machines in all four kitchens had varying amounts of mold growth on inner surfaces. The ice machines in Memory Care, Spring Hill, and Reach had the most buildup. Ensure ice machines are cleaned and sanitized as needed to prevent mold growth.
Equipment such as ice bins and enclosed components, such as ice makers, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.112 Main dish machine rinse gauge was observed at ~198F (almost 200F) during the final rinse cycle. Manager called for service to get the dish machine serviced. 
In a mechanical operation, the temperature of the fresh hot water sanitizing rinse as it enters the manifold may not be more than 194F.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Probes of food thermometers were soiled with stuck on food debris in the REACH kitchen. Food thermometers were cleaned during inspection. Cleaning frequency was discussed. Ensure properly cleaning and sanitizing of food thermometer probes between uses.
Food temperature measuring devices shall be cleaned before use or storage. Clean and sanitize the stems of food thermometers between uses. If alcohol wipes are used to wipe food thermometers, then make sure probes are cleaned and sanitized up to every 4 hours after continuous use.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-102.11 Spray bottles in the Memory Care kitchen were incorrectly labeled as to the contents. Labels were for peroxide disinfectant cleaner and a QT3 product, and both bottles container Re-Juv-Nal quat sanitizer. Contents were emptied from the bottles. Ensure proper labeling of all chemical spray bottles. 
Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 Quat test kit was not available for checking sanitizer solutions in Memory Care kitchen. Test strips were provided. 
A test kit that accurately measures the concentration of sanitizing solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 The following general surfaces were soiled in the Memory Care kitchen:
1. Bottom inside right freezer (food splash); and 
2. Inside cabinet used for storage of cooking spray (general buildup).
Clean inside all fridges, freezers, and cabinets daily/as needed throughout the facility.
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Freshly dispensed sanitizer solution in a sani-bucket was observed at 0ppm quat in the AL memory care kitchen. The chemical jug hooked up at the dispenser was empty. PIC had cook obtain solution from the Summer kitchen until product could be replaced. PIC spoke with a member of housekeeping staff about replacing the product. Housekeeping will educate kitchen staff on where to find replacement product and how to change at the dispenser.  
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Use test strips to verify concentration.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Ice machines in AL memory care, Summer, and Reach kitchens were all observed with mold growth on inner surfaces. Ensure ice machines are cleaned and sanitized as needed to prevent mold growth.
Equipment such as ice bins and enclosed components, such as ice makers, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-502.11 DISH ROOM - Wash gauge on the dish machine was not working. The gauge did not move at all after a half dozens cycles. Call for service was made during the inspection. 
Water temperature measuring devices shall be maintained in good repair and be accurate within the intended range of use.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 Sani-buckets were not setup and available for use in the AL memory care and Reach kitchens. Staff were advised on setup and use of sanitizer solution during hours of operation. 
Sanitizer shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.
